finding_key: packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts::heading memory propagates to every sibling bullet on split, so un-bulleting a list started from a heading turns plain body items into headings
evidence: Verified against block-helpers.ts (~line 260): applySplitBlock retains after.headingLevel for any newBlockType === 'list-item', including an Enter-at-end split that creates a fresh empty bullet; the new test (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:189-207) confirms the new empty bullet carries headingLevel and restores to a heading. Since nothing clears headingLevel when the user types body text into that fresh bullet, un-listing via unlistedBlockType (types.ts:340-348) promotes pure body-text items to headings, exactly as claimed. This propagation is intentional (documented in docs.md and locked in by tests), but the described surprising behavior — invisible heading memory riding onto newly created sibling bullets and converting user-typed body text into headings on un-list — is genuinely present in the code as written.
